article_title: Home Economics in the Service of International Co-operation
brief_extract:
Home Economics in the Service of International
Co-operation

by MARY GEORGE, MBE, Companion IEE, Director EAW

THIS was the theme of the International Congress on Home Economics which took place at Bristol in July and was attended by one thousand delegates from some sixty countries. But what is home economics?

title: Miss
associated_organisation: UK Federation for Education in Home Economics
brief_context: Defined home economics at an EAW Annual Luncheon.
article_title: Home Economics in the Service of International Co-operation
brief_extract:
It is a title not as familiar in this country as in the United States, but it is one which is now in official use. Home economics explained
The internationally recognised definition was given by Miss Frances Laidler, President of the UK Federation for Education in Home Economics, when she was speaking at our EAW Annual Luncheon in Scarborough last May. 'Home Economics today', she said, 'is the study of the family, the home and the community, in-cluding food, clothing, shelter, human relation-ships, which is very different from the old under-standing concerned as it was with the skills of cookery, laundrywork and housewifery'.
